prerequisites: BASIC KNOWLEDGE OF PHYSICS, MATHEMATICS, THERMODYNAMICS AND PRINCIPLES OF APPLIED ECONOMY.

learning_outcomes.text: Illustrate the specific aspects of the process industry with regard to the operation of the production plants and their utilities use, and the appropriate management techniques.
Discuss the main environmental and safety regulations.
Understand heat and material balance concepts and utilization techniques in the implementation of operation in the plants.
Know how to identify the terms of greater technical, economic and safety impact in a process plant.
Know how to expose clearly and technically correctly arguments related to the operation in a process plants.
Know how to read a process diagram.
Know how to apply the competences acquired in contexts different from those treated in the course.

syllabus_topics: THE PROCESS INDUSTRY: DEFINITION AND SPECIFICITY, THE PROCESS AND SERVICE STREAMS
UNIT OPERATIONS IN THE PROCESS INDUSTRY AND DESIGN AND OPERATING VARIABLES, ANALYSIS OF DEGREES OF FREEDOM AND COST EVALUATION OF A PLANT
CIRCULATION OF GASES, SOLIDS AND LIQUIDS
THE DESIGN OF A PROCESS PLANT: FROM IDEA TO DESIGN TO CONSTRUCTION. PLANT DIAGRAMS
MATERIAL BALANCES: METHODOLOGY, APPLICATIONS AND PRACTICAL EXAMPLES
ENERGY BALANCES: USE IN DEFINING UTILITY REQUIREMENTS
INTRODUCTION TO ENVIRONMENTAL AND SAFETY REGULATIONS
assessment_rules: The examination involves an interview to check the ability to set material balances on process equipment, the understanding of safety problems on equipment and process plants, and the understanding of project management and activity plans. The first phase of the exam requires the resolution of an applicative problem. The identification of the solution method constitutes the element to evaluate sufficient preparation. Knowledge of environmental and safety aspects and project management techniques are evaluated with attention to technical understanding, synthesis capacity, and property of terminology. A student who correctly solves the problem and proposes a clear and correct exposition of other required topics is evaluated as excellent.
